---
title: "AI assistant"
---

The assistant understands requests such as "show me the noise of S3 and compare it to the
LNM" and runs the corresponding onthesignal functions (here `lnm(S3)`), then interprets the
results.

## Configuration

```toml
# onthesignal.toml
[ai]
provider = "ollama"          # "anthropic" (Claude), "openai" (ChatGPT) or "ollama" (local)
model = "<model name>"       # mandatory for openai and ollama
base_url = ""                # e.g. http://localhost:11434 for a remote Ollama
auto_execute = "read_only"   # "read_only": analyses run without asking; "none": always ask
send_raw_data = false
```

API keys come from the environment only: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Install the
clients with `pip install -e ".[ai]"`. `/model anthropic` or `/model ollama qwen2.5` changes
the provider for the session.

## Use

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/ai` | toggle the AI mode: inputs go to the assistant (`/ai` again to go back) |
| `/ai <question>` | one question |
| `/init [folder]` | summarize every signal (and the miniSEED files of a folder) into `.onthesignal/init_context.md` |
| `/context` | edit `context.md` (bench, digitizer settings, expected performance...) |
| `/ai_script <name> "<description>"` | generate a script from the template; review it with `/edit_script` |
| `/gen_ai_doc` | regenerate `docs/ai/agent.md` |

## What the model receives

- rules and conventions, and the list of functions with "when to use" phrases (from
  `agent.md`);
- your `context.md` (and `~/.config/onthesignal/context.md`), the `/init` summary;
- the list of signals and results of the session;
- tool results as **summaries** (values, warnings) — never the raw samples.

## Safety

- Analyses and inspection tools run without confirmation (`auto_execute = "read_only"`).
- Running a script, writing a report, running Python code proposed by a model without tool
  calling: always asked first, the code being shown.
- No system command is ever run. Every AI action is logged in the session history.
- With Ollama everything stays on your machine.

## Limits

The model interprets numbers it is given; it can still be wrong. Check its conclusions against
the tables and figures, and review every generated script before running it.
